title: Clopen triviality locus for a doubly rigidified family on two smooth affine varieties
statement:
Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field]. Let $U$ and $V$ be affine schemes of finite type over $F$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-finite-type-morphism] which are smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and geometrically integral [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], meaning integral after every field extension. Fix $F$-rational points $u:\operatorname{Spec}F\to U$ and $v:\operatorname{Spec}F\to V$ [def-pc-rational-point]. Let $T$ be a smooth separated finite-type geometrically integral $F$-scheme; separated means its diagonal is a closed immersion. Let $M$ be an invertible module on $U\times_FV\times_FT$ [def-sc-invertible-module, def-pc-fibre-product]. Suppose its tensor pullbacks [def-pc-module-pullback] to $\{u\}\times_FV\times_FT$ and $U\times_F\{v\}\times_FT$ are trivial, where trivial means isomorphic to the structure sheaf. There exists a field extension $K/F$ [def-pc-field-extension] which is finite, meaning that $K$ is finite-dimensional as an $F$-vector space, such that the following holds. Write $U_K,V_K,T_K$ for the base changes to $K$, $M_K$ for the tensor pullback of $M$, and for $t\in T_K$ let $(M_K)_t$ be its pullback to $U_K\times_KV_K\times_K\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$, where $\kappa(t)$ is the residue field [def-weil-residue-field]. Then
$$E(M_K)=\{t\in |T_K|:(M_K)_t\cong\mathcal O_{U_K\times_KV_K\times_K\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)}\}$$
is open and closed in the underlying topological space of $T_K$.

source.place: Proposition 5.2, proof of Claim 5.2.1, paragraph defining E and asserting its clopenness using normal projective compactifications and see-saw (printed pp.12-13 in March 31, 2026 author version). Smooth affine specialization of the two-factor rigidified-family input. Read online; local copy WANTED. No Stacks tag is claimed to state this nonproper two-factor result.

proof.text: Choose an algebraic closure $k$ of $F$. Smoothness survives all field extensions and products: use smooth base change and composition. Geometric irreducibility survives products, while smoothness gives geometric reducedness and normality. Thus $X=U_k\times_kV_k$ and $T_k$ are geometrically integral, and $T_k$ is normal. They and $X\times_kT_k$ are locally Noetherian, since they are of finite type over a field. The projection $f:X\times_kT_k\to T_k$ is smooth, hence flat, and of finite type; every residue-field fibre is nonempty and integral. The point $(u,v)$ supplies a section $s$ of $f$. These are exactly the hypotheses needed later for generic-line pullback.

source.place: Guo Proposition 5.2, proof of Claim 5.2.1, printed pp.12-13: perfect-closure reduction and the paragraph asserting clopenness via normal projective compactifications and Picard theory; supporting the historical alteration/Picard route beneath det-thm-sf-ctf-stability-direct-images, proof (3).

proof.text: If $M_k$ has no trivial fibre over any algebraically closed extension of $k$, take $K=F$: an actually trivial residue-field fibre of $M$ would remain trivial over an algebraic closure containing $k$, a contradiction. Thus $E(M)$ is empty. Otherwise choose an algebraically closed extension $\Omega/k$ and a point $a\in T_k(\Omega)$ with $M_a$ trivial. Write $Q=\kappa(\eta)$ for the generic field of $T_k$. Choose an algebraically closed field $\Lambda$ containing both $\Omega$ and $Q$ over $k$ (take an algebraic closure of a residue field at a prime of the nonzero ring $\Omega\otimes_kQ$). Let $b\in T_k(\Lambda)$ be the generic point with this field embedding. The scheme $T_\Lambda$ is smooth (smooth base change), of finite type (finite-type base change), separated (its diagonal is the base change of the closed immersion $\Delta_T$, and closed immersions are stable under base change), and integral by geometric integrality, hence connected. Likewise $U_\Lambda,V_\Lambda$ are smooth, affine, of finite type and geometrically integral over $\Lambda$. The two points $a,b$ of the smooth connected separated finite-type scheme $T_\Lambda$ show, by the definition of algebraic equivalence, that $[M_b]-[M_a]$ belongs to $\operatorname{Pic}^{\mathrm{alg}}(U_\Lambda\times V_\Lambda)$. Since $M_a$ is trivial, the product lemma gives $M_b\cong p_U^*A\otimes p_V^*B$.

proof.text: Restrict this exterior tensor expression to $\{u\}\times V_\Lambda$. Its class is $[B]$, since $A_u$ is a one-dimensional vector space over the field $\Lambda$ and hence trivial. The axis hypothesis gives $B\cong\mathcal O$. Restriction to $U_\Lambda\times\{v\}$ similarly gives $A\cong\mathcal O$. Therefore $M_b$ is actually trivial. Apply field-extension detection with the algebraically closed constant field $k$, the smooth affine geometrically integral scheme $X$, and the tower $k\subset Q\subset\Lambda$. It gives $M_\eta\cong\mathcal O_{X_Q}$.

source.place: Guo Proposition 5.2, proof of Claim 5.2.1, printed pp.12-13: perfect-closure reduction and the paragraph asserting clopenness via normal projective compactifications and Picard theory; supporting the historical alteration/Picard route beneath det-thm-sf-ctf-stability-direct-images, proof (3).

proof.text: The generic-line pullback theorem, with all geometric hypotheses checked in step 1, gives $M_k\cong f^*N$ for an invertible module $N$ on $T_k$. Pulling back by $s$ gives $N\cong s^*M_k$. The latter is trivial, since $s$ factors through either trivial axis. Hence $M_k$ is globally trivial on $U_k\times_kV_k\times_kT_k$.

source.place: Guo Proposition 5.2, proof of Claim 5.2.1, printed pp.12-13: perfect-closure reduction and the paragraph asserting clopenness via normal projective compactifications and Picard theory; supporting the historical alteration/Picard route beneath det-thm-sf-ctf-stability-direct-images, proof (3).

proof.text: The finite intermediate extensions $F\subset K\subset k$ form a directed set: a compositum is finite, and every finite subset of the algebraic extension lies in one of them. Their spectra have limit $\operatorname{Spec}k$. Taking the product with $Z=U\times_FV\times_FT$ gives $Z_k=\varprojlim_K Z_K$: on affine charts this is the identity $A\otimes_F k=\varinjlim_K(A\otimes_FK)$, and these identifications agree on overlaps. Each $Z_K$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, being separated and of finite type over a field; the transition maps are affine, being base changes of maps between field spectra. The modules $M$ and $\mathcal O_Z$ are finitely presented, since locally both are free of rank one. Apply the finite-presentation isomorphism descent theorem to the global trivialization in step 4 and its inverse. For some finite $K/F$ this gives $M_K\cong\mathcal O_{Z_K}$. Every residue-field fibre is now trivial, so $E(M_K)=|T_K|$, which is open and closed.
